summary: I could not refute any identity or capability fact in the record. I re-read each one from primary sources on 2026-11-15: the HF API, config.json, README.md, chat_template.jinja, hf_quant_config.json, the ornith.ai blog, the Ollama page and registry manifest, and the vLLM v0.33.0 source. These all match exactly: createdAt 2026-08-18, the param total 9,653,104,368, the 19.31 GB shard sum, every architecture value, 262,144 context, the MIT tag with a LICENSE link that returns 404, thinking on by default with the enable_thinking toggle at template lines 143-150, and Qwen3-Coder XML tool calls. In vLLM v0.33.0, qwen3_xml and qwen3_coder both map to Qwen3EngineToolParser. Every benchmark value and setting matches the card. All of them are vendor self-reported by an unverified HF org, and BenchLM only repeats them. The corrections are minor: deep-reinforce.com redirects to ornith.ai rather than serving it; the Terminal-Bench settings also used top_p=1.0; Ollama's 122b-nvfp4 tag is MLX; the record omits the Ornith-1.5-9B-Mobile variant and the card's other benchmarks (HLE, GPQA 86.4, BrowseComp, WideSearch, SWE Atlas QnA); and the DFlash repo dates from 2026-09-20. Gaps: I did not re-verify the llama.cpp chat.cpp line references, the Ollama and llama.cpp thinking-toggle docs, the GitHub issues, or the memory arithmetic. Who is behind Ornith AI and the actual license text are still unknown. Scratch reads are in $SCRATCH/ornv/.
